reports.evidence: Independent solve: two equal-amplitude waves at phase difference pi/2 give I = 4 I0 cos^2(pi/4) = 2 I0, not I0 - so assertion A ('resulting intensity equals the intensity of one wave') is FALSE. Reason R ('resultant intensity is always the sum of individual intensities for non-zero phase difference') is also FALSE in general (at phi=pi the resultant is 0; at phi=pi/3 it is 3 I0). Both A and R false, and the option set has no both-false answer, so the question has no valid option as written - taxonomy 'unsound', human-only. Stored key D is wrong, and the stored solution uses an incorrect formula I = 2 I0 cos^2(phi/2) (a factor of 2 short), derives I = I0, then contradicts itself by concluding (d). An earlier draft of this analysis adopted that same wrong formula and proposed key C; independent re-derivation from the original question caught it before publishing. Faculty must rewrite or withdraw the question; no auto-edit is safe.
reports.student_reply: Thanks for digging into this one. We re-derived the interference maths carefully: at a pi/2 phase difference the resultant intensity is 2 I0, and the reason statement is not true in general - so as written, none of the four options is fully correct. We have sent the question to our faculty team to fix or withdraw, and your report is what pushed it to the front of the queue.
